headline: This Portuguese island is a world of volcanoes
dek: Crater lakes, Atlantic cliffs and tea fields
editorial_intent: Tell one coherent volcanic island story; test a specific country-led discovery hook against recent generic landscape lists.
reader_scenario: Travellers seeking a future nature-focused island trip.
share_reason: Seven distinctive named stops that form a practical starting point for a São Miguel holiday.
slide_count_rationale: Seven geographically distinct scenes plus required brand card; improve any dull candidate or crop before booking. Brand ending uses slides 1, 4 and 7, none share-alike.
caption:
A volcanic island in the Atlantic, with a crater lagoon offshore and steaming ground inland. 🇵🇹

📍 Vila Franca do Campo — A volcanic islet hides an almost circular lagoon just offshore.
📍 Sete Cidades — Look across twin crater lakes from the Vista do Rei viewpoint.
📍 Gorreana — Walk between sculpted rows of tea bushes on the island's north coast.
📍 Lagoa do Fogo — Look into a mountain crater filled with clear water and steep green slopes.
📍 Ribeira dos Caldeirões — Follow paths through a lush waterfall park in the island's northeast.
📍 Ponta do Sossego — Find a clifftop lookout above the Atlantic on the island's eastern edge.
📍 Furnas — Watch steam rise from volcanic ground in a geothermal valley.

Save São Miguel for a nature-filled island escape. Check seasonal access to the islet before travelling.

Photos: Luís Eusébio, Colin Watts & Nuno Antunes / Unsplash. Ravi Sarma, “Lagoa do Fogo” / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Jules Verne Times Two / julesvernex2.com (Gorreana tea fields; Ribeira dos Caldeirões Waterfall) and Kritzolina (View from Miradouro da Ponta do Sossego 01) / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/.
